claims.claim: Matchmaking places new players against opponents with high prestige levels and hundreds or thousands of hours of experience.

citations.review_text:
Game is clearly designed about never getting new players as the onboarding is nonexistent apart from the regular "use wasd to move, here is how you kill an enemy, good luck" BS. After that you are thrown into lobbies with players with hundreds of hours straight away.

But at least they show you the brand new battle pass before you get into your first round.

Trainee mode ends at bloodline level 11 and that's when you stop going against bots, by then you would have over 2h of the game which makes it so you can no longer refund it.

The problem is that despite being low level you will get matched with people who have prestiged like 7 times or more (prestige = reached bloodline level 100). So you have freshies level 11 going against dudes who have hundreds of levels more compared to you. MMR is a thing, but at one star I've been matched with 3-4 stars before (6 stars is max), and having played many other competitive games before, this is the first game that matchmaking is an actual issue.

I understand that the game is niche but that doesn't change the fact that the problem exist.

Cool premise and gun play however the matchmaking is so horrendous you will want to turn your gun on yourself 5 minutes in. Completely new player getting matched against prestige 19 chuds making it unplayable

Bought the game today and every single person i died to had played this game for thousands of hours when I'm just trying to learn. Prestige 50 hiding in a tent boom one shot. You want to learn? 45 unemployed max level losers in bushes and tents waiting for you. Game needs better matchmaking I cant compete with thousands of hours when I don't have time to learn anything about the game because I'm put against 30 year old bald sweaty losers in their mothers basements.

Started playing the game with a buddy, we notice you play vs. bots.
We both max out the starting character and get pushed to rank 18 ???
Suddenly we get matched with high MMR players and can't do ♥♥♥♥ cause we have 0 equipment like they do, no perks no nothing.

Matchmaking is just broken, we play vs. people who are on high prestige ranks while we have a few hours played in the game.

Issues i found in the game in the first 14 hours while playing with a friend:

-paid outfits are darker than the free ones, often dlc locked too
-You will go agaist people who have 500 hours in the game, because there is no matchmaking, everyone goes into the same match regardless of their knowledge, rank or skill

Honestly I wish this game could be fun for me but the matchmaking is a joke and the lobbies are never balanced, you always get one guy cheating or just running around hard meta in low level lobbies with 20+ prestige under their belt.
It's a slog and it can't even begin to be fun because the second you finish the tutorial you get no-lifers like this ruining every possible lobby you could get

One of the most unfair sweat lord games I have played so far!

Game design - (10/10) Beautiful art style skins for characters look cool and some out of this world cool.

Sound design - (10/10) Its perfect every loud noise comes with a cost same with movement.

Gameplay - (6/10) It feels good in some parts and other times it is a little bit overwhelming and feels to clunky/ floaty feeling with people jump spamming and shooting.

Matchmaking - (MMR) 0/10 Absolutely non existent. (Although they are supposed to be working on this)

The matchmaking system is so bad that it generally ruins it for me, I am prestige 0 level 39 fairly new to the game on steam and I am always being put with teams of prestige 100 level 100 characters every match is just a race to finding the bounty then camping and being shot in the back by a bush camper it annoys me so much! 

Community 2/10? Maybe I have had bad luck with the people I play with on it but some of these random players the matchmaking puts me in with take this game WAY to much! It is usually mostly these prestige 100 sweat lords though! 

Easily a fun game if you enjoy making rage people mad I suppose.. I have had so many people raging in the in game voice chat at me even with me being level 39 trying to learn the game like damn ya'll aughta need to go relax and chill out maybe go touch grass!  HAHA

Crazy how the rest of the game is amazing but the actual balance and matchmaking itself is so unfair.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's sound design and audio cues for locating other players.

citations.review_text:
Easy to learn, hard to master. Excellent sound, great music, incredible atmosphere - I actually feel repulsion towards The Spider boss.
The CRYENGINE is unmatched in rendering nature and open spaces.

The gun handling is really really good. You have single action, double action, one-shot, repetition and semiautomatic weapons.
For some weapons you will have one missing bullet because it is actually loaded into the barrel by the gun's mechanics (which is what happens in real life)
For better handling you'll have to go to Ready or Not, Gray Zone Warfare, Operator, (the great) ARMA.

Also, this game has an incredible feeling of fox and hounds. The sound design is fantastic and usually you can figure out where the players are. But this also means that explosions, loud noises will mask the movement of a player and everything turns into a play of who can make the other guy miscalculate shots and positions.

So I got into this game after trying out ARC Raiders and Marathon.

I could not bring myself to shoot another player in ARC Raiders. For me that game is too social and the world does not make sense for players to shoot each other - thankfully there are the CareBear lobbies :D
Most of the hunters here are very very evil persons so I have no issue in shooting a player in the back - actually after a while you won't care about the bounties, you just want to hunt other players.

Personally I think this game works as PVP because if you are skillful enough you can one-shot a veteran player (headshots FTW) - which does not apply to Marathon because the purple shield is impenetrable by a white weapon. 
Hunt also does not have weapon mods which reload the weapon while holstered or some crazy stuff like that.

#rise-up-dead-man

Going in, you should know that this game is extremely hardcore.

There are almost no second chances, suboptimal gameplay gets shut down extremely fast, and the entire map is designed to rat out your position.
The matchmaking is based entirely on, nothing else. That means that you will be sent into a match with people that have thousands of hours, putting you in a natural disadvantage every game if you are new.
That said, the gameplay itself is wonderful. The world is immersive, the sounds are implemented well, and the graphics are awesome. The guns are balanced - whenever by the damage, velocity, accuracy or price. There is no unfair weapon in this game.
Even the cheapest 25 bucks revolver can one-shot to the head, which makes this game more skill dependent than money dependent. That characteristic is really attractive, since domination through wealth is something that most other extraction shooters struggle with.

I would recommend this game to people that already have a lot of experience with various PVP shooters, or to those that have the grit to push through irritating, unforgiving and unfair matches at the start. 

Pass the whiskey.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that high MMR lobbies are plagued by cheaters using wallhacks and aimbots.

citations.review_text:
This is one of my favourite games of all time. I have lots of positive things to say about the core gameplay. The issue is that you can't and won't enjoy it because the game is completely plagued by cheaters. Whole clans who blatantly admit to cheating in game and on their steam profiles run rampant in high MMR matches. They display KDA's and headshot stats that are obviously obtained through cheating. I have played long enough to make these accusations. Whether it's soft cheating (through wall ESP, radar etc.) or blatant aim-lock cheats, you will experience it, you will be frustrated about it, and it will happen again and again.

The problem is Crytek. Their ineptitude with managing cheating needs to be studied. Crytek is spitting and laughing in the face of their paying customers. I have played many, many hours on this game and feel completely abandoned by thier "developers." Anti-cheat doesn't exist, they don't ban cheaters, and your in-game reports likely get instantly deleted and never reviewed by anyone. There's no feedback system to reporting, and you will find yourself reporting the the same people over and over again with no action. 

Crytek will take your money and laugh at you. They don't care about you, they just want your money. They don't care about the state of their game because they don't play it. Hunt Showdown is borderline unplayable and Crytek hasn't even admitted that the game is in a cheating crisis. Crytek is incompetent and needs to spend less time on in game microtransactions and battle-passes and invest more into an actual anti-cheat system.

Don't get me wrong, it is an amazing game when it is fair. Unfortunately every single lobby in High MMR has a cheater, and you will get used to the clans that blatantly cheat. You will die from the same people over and over again through wall with 0 intel, first shot headshots. I can not recommend this game in this state, get a damn anti-cheat Crytek...

I love this game so much, but sadly I will now stop playing for the time being after almost 3.8k hours and spending easily over 500–700 euros.
Six‑star lobbies in Europe are a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥… hackers, ping abusers, and so on. In almost every round, enemy players seem to smell you from five miles away.
This game has so much potential and so much to offer, but getting demolished every round by extremely suspicious players is no longer bearable.

Don’t get me wrong: I’m completely fine with losing a fair gunfight, getting shot from behind, or being third‑partied. But dying to players who see you for 0.1 seconds and land the most questionable shots is just not okay.
I’ve been a six‑star player since before the 1896 update, and I know six‑star lobbies are sweaty — but not like this, not like in the last couple of months.

You can report players in‑game and on Steam, but it doesn’t matter. They can just keep playing without facing any consequences.
Sometimes they are even showing their cheats on their Steam Page for everyone to see.
And no, it shouldn’t be that the only way Crytek looks into hackers is when you report them through their website. That is pathetic in 2026, in my opinion, if that’s the only real way to get these players banned.

What would help the game?

Ping limit / region lock

Active devs who actually investigate suspicious players and ban them

It could be so simple, but it seems like Crytek doesn’t really care.

As far as I know, these problems are much more common in six‑star lobbies and less so in lower‑star brackets.
So if you’re new to the game or still in lower‑star lobbies: enjoy it, and hope you never reach six stars — they will ruin your Hunt days.

I have almost 4,000 hours in this game. It was by far my favorite game of the last 5 years.
Unfortunately it is now rampant with cheating, macro-using, exploit-abusing players that have gone unchecked for years. I did my part- I recorded, emailed, talked with support, and still run into the same cheating users over and over.
Crytek refuses to address this problem- not for months, BUT YEARS. They love getting up on their social-media platforms announcing their fair-play taskforce and 'we hear you,' but its just a bladder of hot air.
Save your money and the pain of playing a PvP game where you're just going to get stomped on. Go buy something else.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from optimization issues, poor graphics, and high CPU load following engine updates.

citations.review_text: This game provides an incredible take on first-person shooters, with a great atmosphere to the game. The major downside is the inability for the game developers and staff to handle blatant cheating. For a game that is already dying you would think they would take more time and care into their player base other than making more simple-looking skins and or items solely for the purpose of generating revenue without providing unique or inspiring prospects to the game. The playdough-like graphics and poor optimization even after years after developments showcases the lack of care the team has for player experience. While the guns are truly fascinating and compounds are fairly unique, it is a shame the game offers very little in gameplay variance within environmental constructs of the overall maps and compounds. Events are lasting several months in support of the battle pass, but lack depth to engage players long-term; just enough to keep returning players and the slim potential to attract some new players.  While I have my gripes about the game, I really do think the idea and concept of the world and objectives to be unique and fun to play. One of my biggest issues is the player base. Blatant cheaters and veteran players who have thousands of hours in the game, combined with godawful matchmaking, leads to games where there is little to no battle between teams, and more of a slaughter taking seconds for players to be killed without chance to fight. While this may be a given when encountering players of other skill levels, the inability to provide balanced matchmaking, and in their case, pretending to offer a balanced matchmaking experience, only negatively affects the players experience. This greatly alters the ability for people to truly enjoy the game at their own skill levels due to the mechanics of the game supporting those of higher skill level and MMR regardless of relation to other hunters within the same game.

English:

Huge congrats to the Crytek team; over the last 8 years, you’ve somehow managed to consistently make the game worse under the guise of "updates." You probably thought you were pulling off a revolution by updating CryEngine and sending the CPU load through the roof, but all you did was kick out thousands of long-time players with older systems—or forced the rest of us into this optimization-deprived, disastrous experience. I guess you don't really care about ruining the game as long as you can squeeze more money out of the console market, but hey, did you at least pull it off?

It’s been all these years and you still haven't implemented a detailed analysis system that shows exactly who killed us how, from how many meters, with what ammo, or how we took/dealt damage. We’re literally out here Googling "Hunt map," squinting at screenshots, and trying to calculate coordinates ourselves just to figure out how many meters was the shot that we dealt. It’s unbelievable. At the end of a match, there's zero info, zero detail. We can’t even see a proper breakdown of the damage we dealt. "Your teammate downed this hunter" — Oh, really? Which teammate? How? Even putting that aside, at least let us see the stats for the players we downed: the distance, the weapon, the damage... If you kill someone and then die a bit later, that kill or damage doesn't even show up in the "Damage History." Instead of putting cowboy hats on flying bugs, how about you fix the thousands of "bugs" in this game? If you can't do it yourselves, get some help from players like RachtaZ who have put thousands of hours into this. You’ve even taken away our freedom to just load into a map solo to quietly explore and learn the layout. You break working systems and the UI with every single patch, then spend months "fixing" them and bringing them back in a broken state as if you’re doing us a huge favor. You call this innovation? The "Revive Bolt" move was the peak of this nonsense; it’s a miracle that I…

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's spatial sound design and audio cues, noting how footsteps and gunshots inform tactical decisions.

citations.review_text:
!!!!! YOU SHOULD BUY THIS GAME IN 2026 !!!!!!

After 414 hours in the Bayou, I can confidently say this isn't just the best extraction shooter on the market. It is quite possibly the best game I have ever played. It is a pure dopamine machine.

Here is why Hunt: Showdown stands in a league of its own:

--Brains Over Aim--
In 2026, let's be honest: everyone has decent aim. While raw mechanical skill and flick shots might carry you in other shooters like Counter Strike 2, here, they won't save you if you get outsmarted. Hunt is a high IQ game that heavily rewards positioning, patience, and strategy over mindless running and gunning.

--Near Perfect Balance--
The game is 95% perfectly balanced. Literally every single weapon is viable and deadly if you understand its strengths and use it in the right context. There is no absolute "meta" that you are forced to play.

--The Best Sound Design in Gaming History--
This is the true game changer and what separates Hunt from every other game ever made. The audio is an absolute 10/10. You could almost play this game blindfolded. The spatial audio is insanely realistic. A gunshot echoes exactly how it should whether it’s 25, 200, or 800 meters away. Because it’s a PvPvE environment, every snapped twig, heavy footstep, or aggravated monster serves as a critical sound cue. You have to play attentively. The audio doesn't just immerse you, It decides on what choices your gonna be making next. I've never seen another game utilize sound like this.

--A Solid Community--
The community is surprisingly fantastic (about 80% perfect, which is rare for competitive shooters). If you don't want to roll the dice with randoms, the official Discord is packed with chill people ready to squad up and communicate.

--Respect for the Player (Zero Pay to Win)--
The developers respect your wallet. The graphics are a gorgeous 10/10 (especially with the recent engine updates), and while the DLCs and skins are incredibly well designed, they are 100% cosmet…

[h3]The Bayou Calls[/h3]


Extraction shooters typically breed a specific kind of anxiety: the hoarding complex. Games like The Cycle (rest in peace, though it was never quite my cuppa) and Arc Raiders often turn me into a digital pack rat, leaving me more concerned with stockpiling gear than actually using it. Hunt: Showdown 1896 operates on a distinctly different wavelength, sitting somewhere between a battle royale and a Tarkov-lite to forge a subgenre entirely its own. You don’t scavenge for your kit; you curate it beforehand. You bring exactly what you want to use, provided you can afford the in-game currency to buy it.

That economy is a fascinating engine. For veterans sitting on years of playtime who refuse to prestige, the currency has long lost its meaning. But I am someone who resets the loop. I prestige, and because of that, the economic treadmill remains genuinely engaging. It forces you to interact with the sheer variety of weaponry and the distinct tactics they demand. Yes, there are undeniable meta choices, especially with the game's new loadout system, but Hunt remains remarkably balanced by the great equalizer of a well-placed bullet. Gear does not guarantee survival. There is a specific thrill in taking a "free" hunter into the mud and—through pure skill, positioning, and patience—wiping a trio of players who just spent a small fortune on their loadouts.

Visually, it is gorgeous for a multiplayer title, but the true gem here is the texture of the sound design. I find the audio to be nothing short of phenomenal. It is incredibly rare to play a shooter where you can rely on acoustic cues with unwavering faith. You can sit in the brush and count three distinct sets of footsteps rushing past a compound. From a quarter of the map away, you can listen to a distant firefight, identify the exact firearms the other teams brought in, and make a decision on whether you have the tools to outgun them. claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features a steep learning curve and punishing mechanics requiring patience and strategy.

citations.review_text:
Hunt: Showdown is one of the best and fairest games ever made.

The learning curve can be steep at first, as there are many features and mechanics to explore and master. However, once you understand the basics, you can truly immerse yourself in the beautiful horrors of this gritty world.
Whether it’s the freedom to choose your own playstyle and tactics, or the thrill of the extraction mechanics combined with masterclass sound design, the game offers endless replayability.
The progression system is exceptionally fair. Every week, players get new challenges that reward them with experience and "premium currency." This currency can be earned in various ways and is strictly spent on cosmetic skins and animations (the main in-game currency cannot be bought with real money).

The developer, Crytek, stays in close contact with the community, actively listening to feedback and implementing it into the ongoing development. 
Hunt: Showdown was built for the long haul—a fact supported by its steadily growing player base over the years.

This title is an unpolished gem. It carries imperfections, certainly, but if approached with a composed, deliberate mindset, it reveals itself as a masterwork of tactical design. Those burdened by rigid expectations or an unyielding demand for artificial perfection will fail to appreciate what is truly being offered: a visceral micro-model of real-world friction, harsh constraints, and probabilistic uncertainty.
At its core, this is a cerebral endeavor, tailored for the strategic scholar and the tactician alike. The design respects the player by offering no hand-holding or forgiving safety nets; its steep skill ceiling demands genuine mastery, disciplined squad coordination, and adaptive execution. Victory is never guaranteed. It emerges from navigating stochastic chaos, calculating risks under pressure, and executing flawless tactical maneuvers when the variables align.
The atmosphere is immersive and uncompromising, offering a paradoxical sanctuary: a game whose unyielding brutality temporarily relieves you of the mundane weight of reality by forcing absolute presence. Ignore the superficial detractors who lack the patience for depth. Experience it firsthand, master its mechanics, and embrace the friction.

I can't count how many times the bushes killed me :D
Sometimes you get to play against cheaters with insane K/D and wiped teams and locked accounts. But I still like this game, you can judge by 100% that I did on it.
Hunt has a steep learning curve, but the gunfights are pleasant. So is the PvP and PvE. Some skins may be considered p2w, but it depends on how you look at it, they are just darker which gives some advantage, but I didn't have much of an issue. 

Still, it would be GREAT to see some new content like new bosses maybe? The new map compounds are cool though.

Beautifully crafted extraction shooter that is very challenging and unique. The ONLY downside here is that there is no solo mode other than "Soul Survivor" which is different from the main mode "Bounty Hunt" which means youll need friends to play with unless you're looking to 1v3. 
It is so very rewarding but also very punishing, but its all part of the ride. 

You definitely want to find light hearted and fun people to play with because the challenge tends to get a little dreadful and playing with people that rage all the time will not make it any better. I was definitely one of those people that raged all the time and was a complete party pooper but ive gotten better at managing it.

The theme and aesthetic in general is just cool too. It's a gothic themed cowboy game with freaking zombies and monsters which is SO dope. This game has also taught me discipline and patience as a competitive player and it has helped me get used to MnK as I was someone that played on controller for years.

I find I need frequent breaks but ultimately Hunt: Showdown is such a unique and fun experience and is most definitely worth your money if you're looking for a challenge. Cheers and happy hunting (:
